mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS on 20-day returns falls below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day return during FEDFUNDS < 0.5% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 9.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings weakness, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 9.5% in the last month
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when UNRATE > 9.5% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for UNRATE on 20-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad consumer demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction effect fails: Rank IC for HOUST-RSAFS joint decline on 20-day returns is below 0.03 or average 20-day return during joint decline is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing supply shock (INDPRO growth rate below 0.5% for two consecutive months) reduces industrial output and corporate profitability, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day return during INDPRO growth < 0.5% for two consecutive months is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for INDPRO growth rate on 60-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for HOUST growth rate on 5-day returns is below 0.05 or average 5-day return during HOUST growth is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation, triggering monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when CPIAUCSL annual rate > 2.5% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for CPIAUCSL on 20-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates severe labor market deterioration, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction effect fails: Rank IC for PAYEMS-UNRATE joint movement on 20-day returns is below 0.03 or average 20-day return during joint movement is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate below 2.0% for two consecutive quarters) indicates economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day return during GDPC1 annualized growth < 2.0% for two consecutive quarters is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for GDPC1 growth rate on 60-day returns is below 0.03.
